papers.title: Piecewise Interpretations in Many-Sorted Logic
papers.abstract: Piecewise interpretations, introduced by Visser, generalize ordinary interpretations between first-order theories by allowing formulae to be interpreted using disjoint unions of definable sets. This makes it possible to capture natural constructions, such as the projective completion of an affine plane, but also leads to a notion of equivalence of theories, namely piecewise bi-interpretability. We develop the theory of piecewise interpretations systematically in the many-sorted setting. Each piecewise interpretation induces a semantic dual, a functor between categories of models. In addition, we introduce a syntactic notion of morphism between piecewise interpretations, which likewise has a semantic dual. Using these semantic duals, we collect theories, piecewise interpretations, and morphisms between them into a bicategory, in particular defining a well-behaved notion of composition of interpretations, associative up to coherent isomorphism. As an application, we consider a familiar idea, championed by Quine, namely that one can replace any many-sorted theory with a corresponding single-sorted one by replacing sorts with sortal predicates. We show that this leads to a biequivalence between the developed bicategories of theories with finitely many sorts and single-sorted theories, thereby providing an argument for the dispensability of sorts.

papers.title: Nearly Computable Numbers with Additional Properties
papers.abstract: A real number is called \emph{nearly computable} if it is the limit of a computable sequence of rational (or dyadic) numbers that has the additional property that for any computable subsequence the sequence of differences of consecutive elements converges to $0$ computably. The main result of this article provides methods for constructing nearly computable numbers with additional properties. The main result is proved by an infinite injury priority argument. Using these methods, we construct nearly computable numbers with several different additional properties: - a nearly computable number that is not divergence bounded computable, - for any left-computable number $\alpha$ that is neither in the least nor in the highest Solovay degree, a left-computable, nearly computable number that is Solovay incomparable with $\alpha$, - a nearly computable number $\gamma$ that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers but has the property that for any two left-computable numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$ wih $\gamma=\alpha-\beta$ both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are Martin-L\"of random. We also look at two classes of nearly computable numbers: the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ of differences of real numbers that are nearly computable and left-computable, and the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$ of nearly computable numbers that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers. Both classes form real closed fields, in fact, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is closed under computable functions with open domain that are Lipschitz continuous or differentiable. Finally, we show that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is a proper subset of $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$.

papers.title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
papers.abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $\kappa$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(\mu) := \min \{ \lambda \in \mathrm{card} \colon \mu \leq 2^{\lambda} \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $\mu$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(\kappa)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists \kappa \in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

papers.title: A negative answer to the final question in "Les petits cailloux"
papers.abstract: We consider polynomial-time computation over arbitrary structures, with unit cost for the primitive operations and relations and with nondeterministic witnesses consisting of arbitrary structure elements. We prove that every finite-signature structure with two distinct available elements and containing a binary operation $*$ and total unary operations $L,R$ such that $L(x*y)=x$ and $R(x*y)=y$ satisfies $P\ne NP$. The proof encodes an exponentially long computation in one element. An incorrect transition has a polynomial-size binary address, and hence the existence of an error is an $NBP$ problem. Existence of a correct accepting trace belongs to the mixed second level $\Sigma_2^{S,B}$, with an arbitrary-element existential block followed by a binary universal block. We obtain $EXP\subseteq\Sigma_2^{S,B}\subseteq PH$. A hypothetical equality $P=NP$ would collapse this hierarchy to $P$ and imply $P=EXP$, contradicting a direct deterministic diagonalization over the same structure. A simulation by function graphs extends the obstruction to every jointly injective binary primitive under the same assumptions on equality and available elements. Consequently no unary predicate on Malcev's free binary-tree algebra yields $P=NP$, with or without the projections. In contrast, starting from the author's unary example, we construct five infinite structures with binary operations and $P=NP$. These include an algebra with one binary operation and one constant, an expansion with an associative rectangular-band operation, and an algebra with one binary operation whose every row and column has infinite image.

papers.title: Normality in generalized Rudin spaces
papers.abstract:
In \cite{Kojman2026}, Kojman generalized Mary Ellen Rudin's construction of a ZFC Dowker space to larger cardinals and gave a pcf-theoretic condition ensuring that the resulting spaces are collectionwise normal. A subsequent manuscript by Eisworth, Kojman, Lambie-Hanson, and Marun \cite{EKLM2026} develops the theory further and leaves open whether these generalized Rudin spaces can fail to be normal. We answer this question by proving that, for cardinals $\mu<\delta$ with $\operatorname{cf}(\delta)=\aleph_0$, the generalized Rudin space $X(\mu,\delta)$ is normal if and only if $\operatorname{pp}(
u)<\delta$ for every cardinal $
u\in(\mu,\delta)$ with $\operatorname{cf}(
u)=\aleph_0$. Given this characterization, known consistency results provide consistent examples of nonnormal generalized Rudin spaces.

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: We study how stability and the independence property of the norm formula $\varphi(x,y)=\lVert x+y\rVert$ on a real Banach space relate to the same properties in its complete theory. We construct separable Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ and a separable elementary extension $W$ of $X$. The norm formula is stable on $X$ and has the independence property on $W$, and therefore in $\operatorname{Th}(X)$. It is unstable on $Y$ and has no independence property in any model of $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$. Together with $\ell_2$ and $X\oplus_2Y$, these spaces realize all five possible combinations of stability, instability without the independence property, and the independence property on a space with the presence or absence of the independence property in its complete theory. All five spaces are uniformly convex and $\sqrt3$-isomorphic to Hilbert space. Their norms satisfy the common midpoint estimate $\lVert x\rVert,\lVert y\rVert\leq1 \Longrightarrow \lVert(x+y)/2\rVert^2\leq1-(1/12)\lVert x-y\rVert^2$, and $W$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. The proof for $Y$ uses coordinate truncation and a polynomial bound on threshold patterns for vectors of bounded support. These bounds give finite fat-shattering dimension at each positive scale, from which the complete-theory conclusion follows.

papers.title: Rigid Theories
papers.abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

papers.title: Minimising Disquotational Truth
papers.abstract: We present a new axiomatic theory of disquotational truth based on the theory of positive disquotation PUTB. Formulated in classical logic, PUTB restricts the T-schema to positive sentences and satisfies key epistemic desiderata (semantic conservativity and trustworthiness). However, it fares poorly in proof-theoretic strength compared to reflective truth frameworks. To address this, we propose a new theory of positive disquotation aimed at axiomatizing its least fixed-point model. Without requiring additional resources, we achieve this by incorporating ill-founded reasoning under suitable soundness restrictions, applying the tools of cyclic proof theory to axiomatic theories of truth. The resulting theory, CPUTB, is sound relative to the minimal fixed-point model and proves the same arithmetical theorems as the impredicative theory ID1.

papers.title: Strong Completeness of Provability Logic for Languages of size at most continuum
papers.abstract: We investigate the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ for an infinite set of propositional variables $\mathbb P$ over ordinal spaces equipped with the interval topology $\mathcal{I}_1$. For every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, we consider the set \[ \Gamma_\kappa= \{\Diamond p_\xi:\xi<\kappa\} \cup \{\Box(p_\xi\to\Diamond p_\eta):\xi<\eta<\kappa\}, \] and prove that $\Gamma_\kappa$ has a model on an ordinal space with $\mathcal{I}_1$ if and only if $\kappa\nrightarrow_{\mathrm{ipath}}(\omega)^2_{\omega,<\omega}$. We also prove that if $|\mathbb P|<\mathfrak p$, then $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ is strongly complete with respect to $(\omega^\omega+1,\mathcal I_1)$. Finally, we establish the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ with respect to the same space whenever $|\mathbb P|=\aleph_1$.

papers.title: Covering numbers and pcf theory
papers.abstract: We develop a general technique for deriving covering theorems from pcf-theoretic information by refining sequences of partitions. The method gives a direct proof of Shelah's cov vs. pp theorem and analogous results for diagonal coverings associated with normal ideals and covering modulo arbitrary $\sigma$-complete ideals, where $\sigma$ is regular and uncountable. In each setting, we characterize the covering invariant through pseudopowers, true cofinalities of reduced products of progressive sets, and appropriate notions of cofinality in (possible non-progressive) intervals of regular cardinals.

papers.title: Solovay's Construction via Proof Search
papers.abstract: Solovay's celebrated result establishes the arithmetical completeness of GL by embedding Kripke models into arithmetic. We provide an alternative proof of the arithmetical completeness of GL, in which we instead embed failed proof searches into arithmetic. Our methodology requires only a well-behaved sequent calculus and does not rely on completeness with respect to Kripke semantics or any of its variants. This approach is particularly interesting for logics that do not behave well semantically, such as ER, for which we also provide a new proof of arithmetical completeness.

papers.title: $\mathbb Z$ is Diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 28 unknowns
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with deg $F=4$ and $n=393$. In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=28$.

papers.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails. The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. It does not use the $2$-converse or the $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and employed by OpenAI. We define the rational numbers with square denominator using rational points on certain quadratic twists of the congruent number elliptic curve. The criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, in Smith's formulation, implies that these quadratic twists have analytic rank one. A height estimate for rational points on a fixed quotient of a Shimura curve allows us to express multiplication of elliptic-curve indices. We obtain this estimate by bounding the modular levels of the associated quaternionic abelian surfaces. The level bound is based on a compatible system of Galois representations over $\mathbb{Q}$ with controlled ramification and on Khare--Wintenberger's proof of Serre's conjecture. Green--Tao--Ziegler's theorem on linear patterns of primes supplies the rational solutions needed for a Diophantine model of integer arithmetic.

papers.title: Strong Lyndon Interpolation for Multi-Modal Logics with Converses: A Constructive Approach with Tree Sequents
papers.abstract: Grammar logics with converses are multi-modal logics that generalize tense logics and whose frame conditions are determined by context-free production rules. We study the strong Lyndon interpolation property (strong LIP) for these logics, which requires interpolants to respect both the polarities of propositional atoms and the indices of modalities. We show that the strong LIP properly strengthens the Lyndon interpolation property over grammar logics, since it fails for certain grammar logics with bridge axioms, i.e., path axioms relating modalities with distinct indices. We then prove that every bridge-free grammar logic, possibly extended with seriality axioms, has the strong LIP. This class includes the multi-modal tense logics obtained by imposing any combination of seriality, reflexivity, transitivity, symmetry, and Euclideanity on each pair of converse modalities. Our proof is constructive and purely syntactic, and is based on tree sequent calculi. Because standard methods for computing interpolants with tree and nested sequents may introduce modalities whose indices are not common to both sides of an implication, we introduce a novel tripartite partition method. It sorts the labels of a proof into common labels and labels private to the left or right component, and only lets relational atoms pointing to common labels contribute modalities to interpolants. Given a proof of an implication, our method computes a strong Lyndon interpolant together with proofs of its correctness.

papers.title: Strict $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-triangulation of subanalytic sets in low dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a real closed field expanded by an o-minimal structure, let $A$ be a definable, closed and bounded subset of $R^n$ and let $p$ be a positive integer. It was recently shown in \cite{pa2} that $A$ admits a strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation $({\mathcal T},h)$, i.e., there exist a finite simplicial complex ${\mathcal T}$ in $R^n$ and a homeomorphism $h:|{\mathcal T}|\to A$ that is definable and of class ${\mathcal C}^p$. The aim of this article is to analyze a generalization of the notion of strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation of subanalytic sets to the case $p=\infty$. Examples in dimension $n=3$ show that such a generalization is not always possible within subanalytic geometry, where the class ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ is equivalent to the class ${\mathcal C}^\omega$. We formulate the conjecture that strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulations of subanalytic sets always exist in the wider o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, generated by subanalytic sets and the exponential function. We check the conjecture for all subanalytic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n\leq 3$, and prepare tools to address the conjecture for arbitrary $n$. We also apply the obtained strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulation results to approximate subanalytic continuous mappings $f:X\to Y$ between subanalytic sets $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-mappings $g:X\to Y$ definable in the o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, with respect to the strong Whitney ${\mathcal C}^0$ topology. If the continuous mapping $f:X\to Y$ is not necessarily subanalytic, we can still approximate it by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ mappings $g:X\to Y$.

papers.title: Free Gödel algebras over Gödel hoops
papers.abstract: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from G\"odel algebras to G\"odel hoops. If $H$ is a G\"odel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the G\"odel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a G\"odel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary G\"odel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of G\"odel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of G\"odel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between G\"odel algebras and G\"odel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic without tests does not have Craig Interpolation
papers.abstract: It was shown recently by Borzechowski et al. (2026) that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has Craig Interpolation. Whether test-free PDL, i.e. PDL without the `?' operator, has interpolation remained open. Here we answer this question in the negative with a counterexample: a test-free PDL validity for which no test-free interpolant exists. The validity only uses one atomic program and the Kleene star, so it implies that the basic modal logic K extended with the reflexive transitive closure does not have interpolation, as previously shown by Studer (2009). The example was originally obtained using LLMs and Lean. We describe our methodology and provide links to all prompts, LLM output summaries as well as the Lean proof.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations for symmetric programming and reasoning
papers.abstract: We develop a mathematical abstraction for uniformly exploiting symmetries in programming and reasoning based on the mathematical proof principle `without-loss-of-generality' (w.l.o.g.). Given: group actions that describe symmetries of the input and the output; and a canoniser, which captures how arbitrary inputs get sent to canonical ones, our construction extends any function from the canonical inputs to the whole domain. We characterise the conditions on the canonisers which guarantee that the construction gives the unique equivariant (i.e. symmetry-preserving) extension. Furthermore, we adapt the construction to a dependently-typed setting, where it captures traditional symmetric w.l.o.g. arguments via the Curry-Howard correspondence. Finally, we extend the construction to algebraic data types, where the symmetries of the constructors both uniquely determine the symmetries of the data type and pave the way for efficient execution.

papers.title: Why should $\mathbb{Z}$ be Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
papers.abstract: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers.

papers.title: On transformations in the Second Painlevé family
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of algebraic relations among solutions of equations in the second Painlev\'e family $P_{II}(\alpha): y''=2y^3+ty+\alpha$, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}$. More precisely, we prove that if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generic solutions of $P_{II}(\alpha_1),\ldots,P_{II}(\alpha_n)$, respectively, and $tr.deg_{\mathbb{C}(t)}\mathbb{C}(t)(y_1,y_1',\ldots,y_n,y_n')<2n$, then for some $i<j$, we have that $\alpha_i\pm\alpha_j\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $y_i=T(y_j)$ for a classical B\"acklund transformation $T$. In particular, the classical B\"acklund transformations are the only B\"acklund transformations in the second Painlev\'e family.
